Laura —

Appreciate the details and the spec sheet. Quick summary of options and constraints from Redwood's side:

1) Term options we can propose in a Private Offer:
   - 12 months (standard): simplest for buyer approvals, auto-activate on acceptance.
   - 24 months: better unit pricing; standard renewal grace 30 days.
   - 36 months: max duration we can include in a single Private Offer payload to AWS; best pricing but requires additional legal review for auto-renew language.

2) Renewal grace / staggered starts:
   - AWS Marketplace itself does not enforce a "grace" window. Practically, we can include renewal and invoicing terms in the offer and coordinate post-expiry grace handling via our billing team (e.g., 30/45-day manual grace), but AWS acceptance flow must still be completed by an authorized buyer.
   - Staggered starts across sub-accounts are possible but typically require separate line items or separate private offers per sub-account. That increases operational overhead but is doable.

3) Buyer approvals (who can accept):
   - On AWS, the account that accepts the Private Offer must be a Purchasing Admin or have delegated purchasing authority. If Acme prefers BU lead + procurement countersign outside AWS, procurement can accept in the Marketplace and we will honor the external countersignature as your internal evidence. We recommend the Purchasing Admin accept in Marketplace to avoid acceptance rejections.

Next steps I suggest:
- Option A: Draft a 36-month Private Offer with renewal grace noted as 45 days (we'll mark this as an exception and route for legal approval).
- Option B: 24-month Private Offer with standard 30-day grace (fastest).

Vanessa - can you confirm whether ops can carve out a 45-day grace in the Private Offer doc, and if Finance is OK with treating a 36-month as a special legal review?

I'll hold off on drafting the DocuSign until we agree the term.

Thanks,
Connor

Connor / Vivek —

Operational notes from Marketplace/Finance:

- AWS only accepts up to 36 months per Private Offer; that's our upper bound. If client requests >36 months we need to split into multiple offers.
- Renewal grace windows are not enforced by AWS; Redwood can implement a 30/45/60 day post-expiry grace internally, but explicitly calling out a non-standard grace in the private offer is an exception and needs AM + Legal signoff.
- For backdating POs: Procurement can attach a backdated PO as external evidence; acceptance in Marketplace still requires the buyer account to accept on the acceptance date (we can't retroactively change the marketplace acceptance timestamp).

Attachment: pricing_table.csv (contains proposed unit rates for 12/24/36 mo tiers and commit levels).

Action items:
1) Connor: propose which term (24 vs 36) Acme prefers; if 36m, submit "36m + 45d grace" exception request via our internal approval board (I will +1 for strategic accounts).
2) Vivek: if we route through co-sell, coordinate with Amy (AWS PM) to ensure co-sell credits are tracked — we want a clean credit path if Acme accepts a 36m commit.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Programs, Redwood Inference

From: Amy Jensen <amy.jensen@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer questions: term length and buyer approvals

Thanks for the thread — quick clarifications from AWS Marketplace side:

- Max private offer length is 36 months (confirmed).
- The Marketplace acceptance model requires the accepting AWS account to have Purchasing Admin privileges (or equivalent delegated rights). If Acme's BU lead is not a Purchasing Admin, Procurement must accept on behalf of the account.
- "Grace windows" are not a native Marketplace field. Sellers frequently record grace/renewal terms in an external contract (DocuSign) and manage enforcement off-marketplace. That is acceptable, but acceptance still has to come through Marketplace.
- For co-sell credits: file the co-sell case referencing the seller ID and the HubSpot deal id you share; crediting for multi-year commits may require pre-approval depending on the margin profile.

Useful links: 
- Private Offer guidelines: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/help/documents/private-offer-guidance
- Seller co-sell submission: https://partnercentral.aws.amazon.com/co-sell

Happy to jump on a 15m call with procurement if helpful.

Amy Jensen
AWS Marketplace Partner Manager
